discussion_comments.comment_body: True, and worse than it looks: if the client registered its own tool under this reserved name, the interceptor would execute the client's tool as if it were a search. Fixed in a4e8066. The conversion now checks the outgoing tool names first and skips the whole rewrite (body returned unchanged) when the name is already taken. Test added.

Confirmed and fixed in a4e8066. rewriteClaude inserted the search triple early when other tool_use blocks remained, then matched the search block again later, pushing the server_tool_use / web_search_tool_result pair twice for content ordered [client tool_use, search tool_use]. Added an insertedIds set so each search call is emitted exactly once regardless of block order, with the remaining client tool_use preserved at the end. The reversed-order case now has its own test alongside the original ordering test.

Fixed in 46ebf215: incomplete Responses output now suppresses partial tool calls and reports `length` or `content_filter` before considering completed tool calls. Tests cover both truncation reasons with partial tool output.

Fair spec point, but two qualifications: (1) the cited check (isOpenAIResponsesTerminalEvent) inspects chunk.response.status on streaming passthrough chunks — this converter emits non-streaming JSON bodies, and nothing feeds those back into that check (verified: the only .status readers take upstream input bodies, which our own converter always marks completed/failed/in_progress); (2) the derivation is pre-existing logic moved verbatim, not introduced here — this PR only extends it to the forced-SSE path, where it replaces a hardcoded "completed" (a deliberate choice: truncated streams now report truthfully). Mapping length/content_filter to spec "incomplete" + incomplete_details would be a behavior change beyond this PR's scope; happy to do it as a follow-up if you want it.
